basics.name: Ajay Narayanan Sridhar
basics.label: Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Georgia Tech
basics.summary: Research in multimodal AI, retrieval-augmented systems, efficient on-device inference, and contextual bandits for LLM routing. Advised by Prof. Vijaykrishnan Narayanan; expected graduation in May 2027.

education.area: Computer Engineering (Honours), specialization in AI and ML

work.name: Dropbox
highlights: Developed a dense multimodal video retrieval system using CLIP frame embeddings for image- and text-based search at precise timestamps, improving NDCG@10 by 30% over production episode-level retrieval.

Won Best Technical Execution and Most Likely to Ship at the Dropbox Emerging Talent Hackathon 2026 for an end-to-end agentic AI system that triaged customer issues, enriched diagnostics, routed bugs to code owners, and generated JIRA tickets and AI-generated PRs for human review.

work.name: Microsystems Design Lab
highlights: Investigating multimodal retrieval-augmented systems that combine learned embeddings, compact memory representations, and LLM reasoning for question answering and contextual recall over long-horizon user data.

Developing EdgeVQA with QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-VL-3B on VizWiz-VQA and INT8/INT4 (AWQ) quantization for efficient on-device visual question answering, extending NaviSense toward real-time, privacy-preserving mobile deployment.

work.name: Navis LLC
highlights: Designed and developed an Apache Kafka-based, scalable, configuration-driven RESTful machine learning platform for predictive and prescriptive use cases in shipping terminal operations.
Implemented missing-data handling and validation in analytics workflows, delivering 47% faster execution and fewer production failures.

work.name: Navis LLC
highlights: Optimized batch analytics through algorithmic refactoring and pipeline redesign, reducing runtime by 31% for customer-facing reporting workflows.
Implemented ETL failure detection and diagnostics, reducing root-cause analysis time by 40%.

projects.name: Correlation-Aware Contextual Bandits
highlights: Formulated LLM routing as a contextual bandit with correlated arms and surrogate rewards; designed correlation-aware algorithms with regret guarantees robust to surrogate errors while improving regret when surrogates are informative.
Demonstrated up to approximately 15% higher utility across multiple LLM routing benchmarks versus strong online learning baselines and competitive state-of-the-art routing methods.

projects.name: NaviSense
projects.summary: Multimodal AI workflow for real-world task guidance.
highlights: Engineered a real-time multimodal pipeline combining LiDAR depth, visual inputs, and LLM reasoning for grounded, step-by-step task guidance in open-world environments.
Deployed LLaMA 3.2 1B Instruct on-device via ExecuTorch with 4-bit quantization, balancing latency, memory, and response quality for mobile inference.
